title: Lease Decay and Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme
what_it_is: Lease Decay and Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme

sections.label: VERS launch in 20 years
sections.summary: VERS will be launched in about 20 years to pace out redevelopment of older towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: VERS will be launched in about 20 years’ time to pace out the redevelopment of our older towns.

sections.label: VERS eligibility, compensation, voluntary vote
sections.summary: VERS expects more eligible flats, offers less generous compensation than SERS, and is voluntary with residents voting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the case of VERS, we expect more flats to be eligible, as the intention is to space out the redevelopment of the town.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But the compensation terms for VERS will be less generous than SERS, because we will be redeveloping land that is more built up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Hence, VERS will be offered on a voluntary basis and residents will get to vote.

sections.label: Government help for lease end
sections.summary: The Government will help residents get another flat to live in if needed at the end of the lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If they need a place at the end of the lease, the Government will help them get another flat to live in.

sections.label: Studying eligibility and notification timelines
sections.summary: Eligibility and notification timing will be studied, with adequate time given to affected residents when ready for VERS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Residents may be wondering whether their flats are eligible and when HDB will inform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, these are issues that we will study and will take into consideration the timelines and ensuring that if and when we are ready for VERS, we provide adequate time to notify the residents who are affected.

sections.label: HIP extension, second HIP, VERS study
sections.summary: Plans extend HIP, then a second HIP for flats at 60 years, then VERS, with implementation details still to be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First of all, in the more immediate plans, we are talking about extending HIP, which is already a major programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: After that, we are looking at the older flats when they reach 60 years, to do the second round of HIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: After that, we have VERS, and, as I said earlier, we will study how best to go about implementing VERS – the precincts that will be selected, the compensation amounts, the threshold, the mechanism for voting.

sections.label: Voting mechanism for VERS
sections.summary: A resident voting mechanism exists for upgrading, and the best arrangement for VERS will be worked out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do have a mechanism to get residents to vote for upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will see what had been done in the private sector and we will work out what is the best possible arrangement for VERS in order to achieve the outcomes that we want while minimising some of the downsides that the Member has highlighted.
